title: I Built a Database in Rust With Zero Dependencies (and What the Standard Library Quietly Gave Me)
why_read: A beginner-oriented account of building a zero-dependency crash-safe key-value store in Rust, which offers some educational value on what the Rust standard library provides out of the box.
analysis: This is a hackathon write-up about building a minimal database in Rust without any third-party crates, highlighting standard-library features (like file syncing/fsync-equivalents for crash safety) that substitute for common dependencies. It's aimed at beginners and framed accessibly, with some useful discussion of dependency bloat and supply-chain risk stats to motivate the zero-dependency constraint. The technical depth is fairly shallow given the beginner framing and hackathon scope, but it could be a decent quick read for those curious about minimalist Rust systems programming.
